churches.assessment: Calvary Lutheran Church in Jacksonville, NC is part of the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod — one of the most confessionally faithful Lutheran bodies in the U.S. LCMS holds inerrancy of Scripture, justification by faith alone, the bodily resurrection, male-only pastoral ordination, and a Trinitarian creedal Christology rooted in the Book of Concord. The church's "Divine Service" liturgical format (8:00 AM and 10:30 AM Sundays, with Adult Bible Study and Sunday School at 9:15 AM) is the historic Lutheran Mass — Law and Gospel preaching, Word and Sacrament. Located at 206 Pine Valley Rd and serving Marines and families from Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River, this church offers a stable, confessional alternative in a region dominated by Baptist and Methodist congregations. The pastor name is not displayed on the staff page (a link to "Meet Our Pastor" exists but content was not directly verifiable on fetch), so verify pastor on visit. Men's ministry is not visibly advertised — Lutheran congregations often run men's formation through Bible classes and Lutheran Hour Ministries rather than branded "men's ministry" — but worth asking on a visit. Strong recommendation for confessional Lutheran or liturgically-minded Christians in the Onslow County area.

churches.assessment: New City Church SouthPark traces its history to 1973 as Church at Charlotte (EFCA). In 2019 it merged with New Charlotte Church (an Evangelical Presbyterian Church plant founded 2010) to form New City. Senior pastor Jim Kallam served 42 years on staff (37 as senior pastor) prior to the merger — exceptional pastoral tenure. The EFCA-EPC merger is unusual and worth flagging; both denominations are broadly Reformed-leaning evangelical and complementarian, so the merger fits theologically. Charlotte is a thin EFCA metro in the directory, and this is one of the historic anchor congregations for EFCA in NC.

churches.assessment: Sen. Samuel J. Ervin Jr. (D-NC), chairman of the Senate Watergate Committee, was a lifelong member of First Presbyterian Church Morganton, where he served as both Deacon and Elder. Ervin attended the church as a boy and returned to active membership when he retired from the Senate in 1974. His funeral was held at First Presbyterian Morganton in 1985. The congregation honors Ervin's constitutional legacy as a Burke County native son. Currently a PC(USA) mainline congregation under Interim Pastor Rev. Dr. Lance Perry, reflecting denominational shifts that occurred decades after Ervin's formation.

churches.assessment: Hayes Barton Baptist (Raleigh NC) is a 1926-founded congregation dual-aligned with the Baptist State Convention of NC (SBC's NC state convention) and the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship. The senior pulpit is occupied by Dr. David J. Hailey (male), but two ordained women carry the formal title 'Pastor' on staff — Rev. Kristen Muse as Executive Pastor (since 2011) and Rev. Sarah Mears as Associate Pastor of Children and Families and Communication. Muse was interviewed in 2024 specifically as an example of a female SBC pastor whose role would be banned under the Law Amendment that subsequently failed. The use of 'Pastor' (not 'Minister') in formal staff titling places the congregation in direct conflict with BF&M 2000 Article VI while remaining nominally SBC-cooperating.

churches.assessment: Lutheran Church of Our Savior is the ELCA Lutheran congregation on Lejeune Boulevard — the main road between downtown Jacksonville NC and Camp Lejeune. The pastor, Mike Lang, is male, and the congregation likely contains many sincere Christians (including military families). But the denominational frame is the issue. ELCA's 2009 ChurchWide Assembly formally authorized the ordination of partnered same-sex clergy and the blessing of same-sex relationships; subsequent assemblies expanded that posture. ELCA has ordained women at all levels (including bishops) since 1970. The homepage greeting — "ALL are welcome" with open communion ("Holy Communion is available to all baptized Christians") — is consistent with the inclusive/welcoming identity ELCA has cultivated. This is institutional drift from biblical sexual ethics. Per MOOP rubric, ELCA congregations are flagged RED at the denominational level regardless of local pastor or local rhetorical conservatism. churches.assessment: MOOP attended River of Life Church in Jacksonville, NC during V-22 training at MCAS New River, including an Ancient Paths Seminar there. Adam noted it was 'kinda charismatic but seemed solid.' Founded 1992 by Chris and Miriam Phillips after four years as missionaries in Brazil; the congregation began as Living Water Fellowship in a Henderson Drive storefront and was renamed River of Life Church. The husband-wife co-pastorate (with Miriam credited as 'a dynamic speaker and teacher') is a functional egalitarian arrangement that flags RED on the gender axis per MOOP rubric, even though Adam's personal experience attending was positive. Pastor Chris Phillips has a notable heart for military families in the Lejeune/New River community. Overall YELLOW — solid missional posture and a personal positive impression by MOOP, but the egalitarian co-pastor model warrants the caution flag.

Two of its co-planting/founding pastors (Charles McKnight III and Drew Martin) signed the 2020 Warhurst Protest. Both have since transitioned to denominational/academic roles, so the present-day cultural posture is partially decoupled from their tenure but warrants ongoing review under current pastor David Yoran.
